enemy-049-wild-boar-host.name: Wild Boar Host
enemy-049-wild-boar-host.continuityDecision: A living wild-boar host designed for this project. Alien 3 establishes animal-host continuity through a dog in the theatrical version and an ox in the released Assembly Cut; neither work establishes a specific living wild-boar host design. The similarly named Kenner Wild Boar Alien is a xenomorph toy phenotype and is excluded from this host design.

sources.use: Confirms Alien 3 as the licensed work; inspect the theatrical and released Assembly Cut themselves for the dog-versus-ox host distinction. The landing page is not treated as a creature model sheet.
Corroborates the licensed Dog Alien/canine-xenomorph identity only; it is not a reference for the living boar's anatomy or surface.
Name-conflict guardrail only. Never reproduce the Kenner Wild Boar Alien's olive biomechanical/bony xenomorph design.

v56Predecessors.role: project-owned identity predecessor; guidance only, not a V66 source contract
project-owned normalized predecessor; preserve readable identity, do not upscale/copy frames

enemy-049-wild-boar-host.designLock: PROJECT_ADAPTATION: original living natural wild-boar host for Tantalus Frontier, compact low right-facing profile, heavy forequarters, elongated snout, two tusks, four legs, cloven hooves, short tail and bristle ridge; earthy black-umber organic hide only. Alien 3 dog/ox animal-host continuity and the Kenner name are guardrails, never a 1:1 model. Exclude every xenomorph, biomechanical, armored, domestic-pig or fantasy-monster cue.

clips.lockedMotion: Eight grounded phases: settle, inhale, slight ear flick, guarded sniff, exhale and seamless return; no translation.
Eight chronological natural boar run/trot phases with four distinct legs, alternating supports, spine compression/extension and seamless contact cycle.
Eight chronological phases: lower head, brace, short rightward drive, tusk contact, upward shove, follow-through, recoil and guarded recovery.
Eight irreversible phases: lethal impact, front support buckles, momentum carry, shoulder fall, flank roll, limb settle and terminal motionless body; never loops.

acceptanceGates: 4 sheets, each exactly 1774x887 PNG, 4x2 and eight individually authored row-major poses
32/32 cells face right and contain one whole boar without crop, overlap or boundary contact
identity, tusk count, limb count, rigid body scale and hoof ground line remain stable across clips
transparent RGBA or uniform pure #FF00FF chroma only; no scene, shadow, text, grid or watermark
visual reviewer confirms living natural boar host and rejects any Kenner/xenomorph phenotype

designDetails.silhouette: Natural compact low wild boar: heavy forequarters, short neck, elongated wedge snout, small ears, two readable tusks, four short powerful legs, cloven hooves, short tail and continuous dorsal bristle ridge.
designDetails.palette: Earthy near-black and umber hide/fur; desaturated gray-brown bristles; dirty ivory tusks and hooves; restrained warm flesh only at snout/ears.
designDetails.surface: Organic coarse bristles, hide folds, mud and scar wear. No glossy biomechanical carapace, tubing, resin or acid slime.
designDetails.anatomy: One natural boar head, lateral natural eyes, one jaw, two tusks, four mammalian legs, cloven hooves, short non-weapon tail. Living animal host, not xenomorph offspring.
designDetails.orientation: strict orthographic gameplay profile facing RIGHT in every pose; snout and tusks point right, lateral eye visible, camera never rotates
designDetails.scale: Runtime envelope inherited from V56 override: 158 x 88 logical pixels, low quadruped. Hold one rigid body length and shoulder height across all clips; root at the supporting hoof line.
designDetails.grounding: All supporting hooves share one ground line. Airborne phases are allowed only during natural locomotion/attack and must return to that root without drift.
prohibitions: Kenner Wild Boar Alien olive/bony xenomorph phenotype
xenomorph dome, inner jaw, dorsal tubes, acid, blade tail or biomechanical ribs
harness, saddle, armor, fantasy tusk monster or mount
front-facing or left-facing head, perspective turn, duplicate pose or silhouette drift
